name: Committees weighted the same evidence differently
definition: Both committees identified the same strength or weakness of the paper, but they gave it different weight in their recommendations.

name: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive
definition: One committee's reviews were thin or inattentive (little time, few or no weaknesses named, mostly restated claims from the paper), so its scores rest on less scrutiny than the other committee's.

name: Only one committee raised a substantive concern
definition: One committee raised a substantive concern about the paper's claims, method or evidence that the other committee never raised, and that concern counted against the paper in its recommendation.

name: Meta-review dropped the reviewers' stated weaknesses
definition: One committee's meta-review summarised the paper without the weaknesses its own reviewers had named, or stated the opposite of them, so the recommendation rested on a one-sided account of that committee's reviews while the other committee's meta-review carried its reviewers' reservations forward.

name: Higher tier given with no stated grounds
definition: One committee's recommendation reached a higher tier than its scores or its own meta-review supported, and nothing in its record argued for that tier, so part of the split reflects an unexplained tier assignment, not the reviews.

name: Rebuttal moved one committee but not the other
definition: The authors' response persuaded one committee and moved its scores or recommendation, but left the other committee's scores and recommendation unchanged.

name: Score rested on a factual misreading of the paper
definition: A reviewer or area chair on one committee stated a checkable claim about the paper's results that was wrong, overstating or understating them, and that error fed that committee's scores or recommendation.

name: Area chair's own judgement drove the recommendation
definition: One committee's area chair set the recommendation from their own reading or taste, above or below what that committee's reviewer scores and arguments supported.

name: Rebuttal could answer one committee's concerns only
definition: One committee's main concerns were gaps the authors could close in their response with new results or clarification, while the other committee's main concerns were about the paper's scope or demonstration, which no response could fix, so the rebuttal lifted the first committee's scores further than the second's.

name: Non-expert reviewers' accept scores counted in full
definition: Reviewers on one committee who said they could not verify the main results (proofs unread, area unfamiliar) still gave clear accept scores, and the area chair counted them at full weight, which lifted that committee's mean and tier above what its checked assessments supported.

name: Damaging rebuttal admission did not lower scores
definition: The authors' response to one committee conceded an unfavourable fact about the paper's results, such as a stronger baseline beating the method, and that committee's reviewers and area chair did not lower their scores or recommendation, or raised them, so that committee ended higher than its information supported.

name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
definition: One committee required the paper to meet a standard tied to its kind of contribution that the other committee did not apply, such as demanding that an empirical analysis paper yield practical guidance or a method, and counted its absence against the paper, while the other committee valued the contribution on its own terms.

name: Scores rose on unverified rebuttal evidence
definition: One committee's reviewers raised their scores on rebuttal material that was not checked under the paper's own protocol, such as results copied from other papers or promised revisions, which lifted that committee's scores further than the evidence the other committee saw.

name: One committee's reviewers left the rebuttal unanswered
definition: Most of one committee's reviewers never replied to the authors' response or joined the public discussion, so scores set before a response that answered their points stood unrevised, while the other committee's reviewers engaged with the response and revised.

name: Novelty judged against wrong or ignored prior work
definition: A reviewer's novelty verdict on one committee rested on a wrong account of prior work, either citing as precedent work that does not do what the paper does or accepting a 'first' claim that known prior work contradicts, and that verdict fed the committee's score.

name: Authors told the two committees different things
definition: The authors' responses to the two committees differed in substance, such as different result numbers, conflicting accounts of the method or setup, or concessions offered to only one committee, so each committee judged different evidence about the same paper.

name: Reviewer's rating out of line with own text
definition: A reviewer's numeric rating clearly disagreed with the verdict of their own written review, for example wholly positive text with a borderline score, and so moved that committee's average away from what its reviews said.

name: Unanimous scores read as grounds for higher tier
definition: One committee's area chair took the reviewers' agreement, with no dissenting score, as grounds for a higher tier, although no reviewer rated above the accept level or argued for that tier, while the other committee's spread of scores held it lower at a similar or higher mean or maximum.

name: One outlying score set the tier
definition: A single reviewer whose score stood far from the rest of their committee, as champion or detractor, moved that committee's mean across a tier boundary, while the remaining reviewers' scores matched the other committee's.

name: Only one committee had an engaged champion
definition: One committee had reviewers who studied the paper closely and rated it well above the accept level, while the other committee's most positive reviewer gave a light review and did not engage after the rebuttal, so nobody there argued for the paper against its critics.

name: Promised fixes judged too large without re-review
definition: One committee's reviewers or area chair accepted that the authors' promised revisions addressed the paper's faults but rejected it because those revisions were too large to accept without another round of review, while the other committee treated the same fixes as camera-ready changes.

name: Area chair followed one outlying reviewer
definition: One committee's area chair set the recommendation by a single reviewer whose score or view stood apart from the rest of that committee, adopting that reviewer's verdict, often verbatim, and setting the other reviewers' views aside.

name: Recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact
definition: One committee's recommendation rested on a forecast of broad impact beyond the paper's own setting, a forecast that the paper does not demonstrate and the other committee did not make.

name: Reviewer discussion moved one committee's scores
definition: A reviewer on one committee changed their score after reading or discussing the other reviewers' assessments, not the authors' response, which moved that committee's recommendation away from the other's.

name: Late objection left the authors no reply
definition: A reviewer on one committee raised a new objection, or lowered their score, only after the author-response period had closed, so the authors could not answer it and it stood unrefuted in that committee's recommendation, while the other committee's objections came early enough to be answered in the rebuttal.

name: Area chair settled an even split for one side
definition: One committee's reviewers split evenly between accept and reject at similar confidence, and the area chair settled the split by adopting one side's critique without addressing the other side's scores, so the recommendation reflected that side alone while the other committee had no such split.

name: Reviewers placed similar verdicts at different scores
definition: The two committees' reviewers wrote similar verbal assessments of the paper but placed them at different points of the rating scale, and area chairs who set the tier by the mean turned that calibration gap into different recommendations.

name: Area chair relied on off-record reviewer input
definition: One committee's area chair based the recommendation on an assessment that is not in the committee's record, such as an emergency reviewer's or a consultant's verdict, and used it to settle a split that the visible reviews left open.

name: Low score held on a peripheral point
definition: A reviewer on one committee held a below-threshold score after the rebuttal on a point peripheral to the paper's contribution, such as a variant the method does not use or a presentation detail, and that score counted at full weight in that committee's mean and recommendation.

name: Unsure reviewers defaulted to a borderline score
definition: One committee's reviewers, more than the other's, said they could not judge the paper (proofs unchecked, key prior work unfamiliar) and gave borderline scores in place of a verdict, which held that committee's mean near the acceptance threshold.

name: Audience or venue-fit objection lowered one committee
definition: One committee's reviewers or area chair judged the paper sound but too specialised for the conference's audience, or better suited to another venue, and held their scores or tier down on that ground, while the other committee never raised audience breadth or venue fit.

name: Neighbouring-field reviewers contested the paper's framing
definition: One committee's critical reviewers read the paper from the premises of a neighbouring field and objected to its framing or definitions on those premises, not to its technical results, while the other committee's reviewers accepted the paper's framing, and those framing objections counted against the paper.

name: Discarded detractor framed decision as accept-or-reject
definition: One committee's area chair set aside an outlying low score as unreliable but spent the meta-review defending acceptance against it, so that committee's recommendation stopped at a plain accept and a higher tier was never weighed, while the other committee, with no such detractor, was considered for a higher tier.
